item.title: Iran faces economic collapse after 40 days of war
item.description: Iran emerged from 40 days of U.S.-Israeli bombardment this week with a two-week ceasefire in hand but an economy in ruins. In interviews with Iranian political insiders, business owners, and analysts, Reuters charted a country "near the brink of economic collapse," warning that any military gains Tehran secured during the conflict may prove fleeting.

item.title: 289-million-year-old mummy reveals oldest rib-based breathing
item.description: A tiny mummified reptile that died in an Oklahoma cave roughly 289 million years ago has yielded the oldest known evidence of rib-based breathing in amniotes — the group encompassing all reptiles, birds, and mammals — according to a study published Wednesday in Nature.

item.title: Trump sends Vance, Witkoff, Kushner to Islamabad for Iran talks
item.description:
President Donald Trump is dispatching a high-level delegation led by Vice President JD Vance to Islamabad for face-to-face negotiations with Iran, the White House announced Wednesday, just hours after a fragile two-week ceasefire halted 38 days of U.S. and Israeli military operations against Tehran.

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed the team. "I can announce that the president is dispatching his negotiating team, led by the vice president of the United States, JD Vance, Special Envoy Witkoff and Mr. Kushner to Islamabad for talks this weekend," she said. "The first round of those talks will take place on Saturday morning local time."

item.title: Iran’s parliament speaker says cease-fire terms already violated
item.description: Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Wednesday that three clauses of Tehran's 10-point ceasefire framework have already been violated, casting doubt over the fragile truce reached just hours earlier between the United States and Iran. The accusation came as Israel launched what its military called its largest wave of strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon since the war began, hitting 100 targets in 10 minutes.

item.title: UN envoy arrives in Iran amid fragile US ceasefire
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres's personal envoy Jean Arnault has arrived in Iran as part of a regional tour aimed at supporting "a comprehensive and durable resolution" to the conflict engulfing the Middle East, the United Nations announced on Wednesday. The visit comes amid a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran brokered just one day earlier with Pakistan's mediation.

item.title: Vance to lead US delegation in Iran talks in Islamabad
item.description: The United States and Iran are preparing for their first face-to-face negotiations since the outbreak of war, with Vice President JD Vance set to lead the American delegation to Islamabad this weekend for talks aimed at forging a lasting peace agreement. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf will head Tehran's team, according to Iran's semi-official ISNA news agency. The high-stakes diplomacy follows a two-week ceasefire agreed to on Tuesday night, brokered largely through Pakistan's mediation.

item.title: Israeli strike kills Al Jazeera journalist in Gaza
item.description: Israeli forces killed at least 10 Palestinians in Gaza on Tuesday and carried out further strikes on Wednesday, including one that killed Al Jazeera correspondent Mohammed Wishah, as the U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement continues to unravel six months after it took effect.

item.title: NATO chief Rutte meets Trump amid US threat to leave alliance
item.description:
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte arrived at the White House on Wednesday for what may be the most consequential meeting in the alliance's 77-year history, as President Donald Trump's threats to withdraw the United States from the military bloc have plunged transatlantic relations into uncharted territory.

The meeting, confirmed by NATO and the Associated Press, comes after Trump told Reuters and The Telegraph in recent interviews that he is "absolutely" considering pulling the US out of NATO, citing what he called "disgust" with the alliance over European members' refusal to support the US-Israeli air campaign against Iran, launched on February 28. "I was never swayed by NATO," Trump said. "I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way."

item.title: UK vows to restore shipping confidence in Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran ceasefire
item.description:
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper announced on Wednesday that the United Kingdom will work with the shipping, insurance, and energy sectors to restore confidence in the Strait of Hormuz "as quickly as possible" following a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran.

"Iran must cease all mining, drone attacks, and other attempts to block commercial shipping in the Strait immediately," Cooper said in her statement.

item.title: Israel kills 254 in largest Lebanon strikes as ceasefire dispute erupts
item.description: Israel unleashed its most devastating wave of airstrikes on Lebanon on Wednesday, killing at least 254 people and wounding more than 1,160 others in what the Israeli military called its "largest coordinated wave of strikes" since the war began on March 2, according to Lebanon's Civil Defence. The assault, which struck over 100 targets across the country within 10 minutes, came just hours after a U.S.-Iran ceasefire took effect — and amid sharp disagreement over whether Lebanon was included in the deal.

item.title: Iran recloses Strait of Hormuz, threatening U.S. ceasefire
item.description:
Iran shut down the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, less than 24 hours after agreeing to a two-week ceasefire with the United States, casting immediate doubt over whether the fragile truce that ended more than five weeks of war could survive. Tehran cited Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon as a violation of the agreement, while Washington called the closure "completely unacceptable."

The ceasefire, brokered with Pakistan's help and announced Tuesday evening just hours before a deadline set by President Donald Trump, had hinged on what the U.S. described as the "complete, immediate, and safe opening" of the strait — a waterway responsible for roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply. Iran confirmed it would allow passage "in coordination with Iranian armed forces," but Israeli strikes on Beirut that killed more than 100 people overnight appeared to upend that commitment.

item.title: UAE demands Iran pay reparations after 40 days of attacks
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates on Wednesday demanded that Iran be held "accountable and fully liable for damages and reparations" following weeks of devastating aerial attacks, as Abu Dhabi sought clarity on the terms of a fragile two-week ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump.

In an official statement, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the "unprovoked Iranian attacks targeting infrastructure, energy facilities, and civilian sites over the past 40 days — which included 2,819 ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones — and the resulting loss of life and property damage, necessitate a firm position". The ministry said it was seeking clarification from Washington on the ceasefire's provisions to ensure "Iran's full commitment to an immediate cessation of all hostilities in the region and the complete and unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz".

item.title: Artemis II crew to hold press conference from deep space tonight
item.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are coasting back toward Earth on Wednesday after completing a record-breaking lunar flyby, with the crew scheduled to hold their first in-space press conference later tonight as they near the end of a 10-day voyage around the moon.

The 20-minute virtual news conference is set for 9:45 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 8, with NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, answering media questions from roughly 200,000 miles away.

item.title: Trump weighs relocating troops to punish NATO allies over Iran war
item.description:
The Trump administration is considering a plan to relocate U.S. troops away from NATO member countries it views as uncooperative during the Iran war and reposition them in nations that showed greater support for the military campaign, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing administration officials.

The proposal, which has circulated among senior officials in recent weeks and gained backing, remains in its early stages. It is one of several punitive options the White House is discussing to penalize NATO members that declined to assist during the U.S.-Israeli bombing campaign, which began in late February.

item.title: Vance questions Iranian speaker's English as ceasefire rift grows
item.description:
U.S. Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday dismissed Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf's claims that Washington had violated the newly declared ceasefire, questioning whether the senior Iranian official could properly "understand English" and casting the dispute as evidence that the two sides are closer to agreement than Tehran admits.

Vance's combative remarks came hours after Ghalibaf alleged that three of the 10 points in Iran's proposed negotiating framework had already been breached before formal talks could begin — citing Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon, a drone allegedly entering Iranian airspace, and Washington's refusal to recognize Iran's right to enrich uranium.

item.title: Russian warship escorts sanctioned tankers through English Channel
item.description:
A Russian naval frigate escorted two sanctioned oil tankers through the English Channel on Wednesday, in what observers described as a direct challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's threat to seize vessels belonging to Moscow's shadow fleet. The Admiral Grigorovich, a guided-missile frigate armed with anti-ship, cruise, and surface-to-air missiles, sailed between the two tankers as they passed the south coast of England, according to The Telegraph, which reported observing the convoy from a vessel off Dover.

A British Royal Fleet Auxiliary vessel trailed the Russian formation but made no attempt to board or intercept the sanctioned ships. One of the tankers was identified as the Universal.

item.title: North Korea tests cluster warhead on ballistic missile in military trial
item.description: North Korea tested a tactical ballistic missile armed with a cluster bomb warhead as part of a three-day series of weapons trials, state media reported Thursday, capping a burst of provocative launches that drew condemnation from Seoul.

item.title: Pentagon says US ready to resume Iran combat if ceasefire falters
item.description: Hours after a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran took effect, the Pentagon on Wednesday warned that American forces remain prepared to restart combat operations if diplomatic talks collapse, even as fresh Iranian strikes on Gulf Arab states underscored the fragility of the truce.

item.title: Hezbollah vows retaliation as Israeli strikes devastate Lebanon
item.description: Hezbollah condemned what it called Israel's "barbaric aggression" on Wednesday and declared it has the "natural and legal right to resist occupation and respond to its attacks," after Israeli warplanes carried out the deadliest wave of strikes on Lebanon since the current conflict began in March. The statement came hours after an armada of Israeli fighter jets struck more than 100 targets across the country in just 10 minutes, killing over 250 people and wounding more than 1,100, according to Lebanon's civil defense authority.

item.title: Sharif's 'draft' post gaffe raises questions about Pakistan's mediator role
item.description: Pakistan's self-styled role as an independent broker of the US-Iran ceasefire is facing scrutiny on two fronts: a Financial Times report published Wednesday revealing that Washington actively pushed Islamabad to act as a conduit for American proposals, and a viral blunder on social media that suggested Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's diplomatic messaging may have been externally scripted.
